question.text: How long must an AIF retain KYC and transaction records of investors under PMLA (Maintenance of Records) Rules?

answer.text: 2 years from the date of transaction
3 years from the date of KYC update
5 years from the date of cessation of the transactions with the investor (longer if litigation pending)
10 years from the date of fund wind-up

explanation.text: The Logic: PMLA Rules require reporting entities (including AIFs and Custodians) to maintain KYC and transaction records for a MINIMUM of 5 YEARS from the date of CESSATION of the transactions with the client. If any litigation is pending, records must be maintained till the completion of proceedings. Records must enable reconstruction of individual transactions. The Trap: Options A/B understate the retention. Option D (10 years) is the Companies Act 2013 books-of-account retention — different law. The PMLA retention is measured from cessation, not from transaction date. Cross-Exam Context: XXIV AML is the definitive exam. SEBI maintenance-of-records rules for intermediaries (III-A/C) are 5 years — consistent. Banking (RBI KYC Master Direction) also 5 years. Income Tax retention is 6 years (separate regime). Manager's Pro-Tip: For a 10-year Cat II AIF, effective record retention runs 15+ years: 10 years of fund life + 5 years post-wind-up. Budget for secure digital archiving (cloud KMS, access logs). Don't delete on fund-tenure-end — the cessation clock starts from LAST LP redemption, not fund's legal dissolution.
